summary: Enhance your skills in water, sanitation, and hygiene with our comprehensive training course designed for rural communities. Join us to make a difference today!
lede: Rural water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) training is for practitioners planning, delivering, or overseeing services in rural communities. It covers assessing water sources and quality, choosing suitable sanitation approaches, and designing hygiene promotion that supports behavior change. Learners also explore community engagement, inclusive planning, risk management, and monitoring service sustainability and outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals involved in planning, implementing, or overseeing WASH interventions in rural communities.
audience: NGO and INGO WASH program officers
Public health and environmental health officers
Rural water supply and sanitation managers
Government staff in water and health departments
Project and field coordinators in humanitarian settings
modules: Foundations of WASH in Rural Communities
Rural Water Supply Systems and Source Protection
Community Engagement and Ownership in WASH
Gender, Inclusion, and Equity in WASH Programming
WASH, Public Health, and Disease Prevention
Climate Change and Resilience in Rural WASH
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Sustainability of WASH Services
Managing Risks, Failures, and Lessons Learned in WASH Projects
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of public health or community development principles. Prior experience in managing or implementing development projects is beneficial.
